claims.text: EF Core translates a LINQ query into one SQL command and sends it when the query is executed, e.g. by ToListAsync().
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Querying > How queries work

claims.text: After executing a command, EF Core logs an entry (event CommandExecuted, id 20101) under category Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command at Information, with the elapsed time, the parameters and the SQL text.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Performance > Performance diagnosis (Identifying slow database commands via logging); RelationalEventId.CommandExecuted

claims.text: Each log entry has a level; Information is less severe than Warning. Logging:LogLevel maps category names to the minimum level kept, so a category set to Warning drops Information entries.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging in .NET and ASP.NET Core > Configure logging

claims.text: A Logging:LogLevel name matches every category whose name starts with it; when several match, the longest matching prefix is selected, so Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command overrides Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging > How filtering rules are applied

claims.text: By default EF Core does not include parameter values in logs (shown as '?'); EnableSensitiveDataLogging includes them. The default exists because such data may be confidential.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Logging > Simple logging / Microsoft.Extensions.Logging > Sensitive data

claims.text: Parameter values are sent to the database with the command, separately from the SQL text; hiding them in the log does not change what is sent.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Logging > Sensitive data; Querying > SQL queries (parameters); observed with efcore-sql.sh limit=1

claims.text: Sensitive data logging should be turned on only on a developer's machine, because it writes values that may be personal data into logs.
ToQueryString() called on a LINQ query returns a debugging string of the SQL EF Core would send, with each parameter and its value in comment lines above it, without executing the query.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: What's new in EF Core 5.0 (ToQueryString); Logging, events and diagnostics overview

claims.text: DonHang.Api/appsettings.json at stage-2 sets Logging:LogLevel Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore to Warning.
In docker-compose.yml at stage-2 the api service sets Logging__LogLevel__Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command to Information as an environment variable.
In environment variable names read by ASP.NET Core configuration, a double underscore __ is converted to the : separator of configuration keys.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Configuration > Environment variables (double underscore)

claims.text: Environment variables override values from appsettings.json in the default ASP.NET Core configuration, so the compose setting takes effect for its category.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Configuration > Default application configuration sources (order)

claims.text: scripts/backend/efcore-sql.sh signs in as customer 3 (dung.le), requests GET /api/v1/orders?after=5&limit=20, then prints the last Database.Command entry mentioning FROM orders from the api log.
The captured entry shows 'Executed DbCommand (...ms)', parameters @customerId, @afterId, @p each '?', and SQL with an inner query on orders (alias o0) joined to customers outside it.
The number in 'Executed DbCommand (Nms)' is the time the command took to execute.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Performance diagnosis ('The above command took 4 milliseconds')

claims.text: The api service's connection string points at the database donhang on host db.
With limit=1 the response holds only order 6, while the logged SQL text is identical and parameters are still '?' (observed on the stage-2 lab).
claims.source_hint: Run scripts/backend/efcore-sql.sh with limit=1 in the curl line on the stage-2 lab

claims.text: A LINQ query runs in PostgreSQL as SQL EF Core wrote, and the command log says how long that part took, so read the SQL and its time before changing the C#.
From the example repository root, `docker compose exec lab psql --host db --username donhang --dbname donhang` opens psql on the donhang database (PGPASSWORD is set in the lab container).
efcore-sql.sh pipes the matching log line to jq inside the lab container, which prints the entry's level, category, event id and message.
